Context (E : @EquivalenceOfCategories C D F). … Definition equivalence_reflects_isos : ReflectsIsos F := ff_reflects_isos (HF := Equivalence_Full E) (HfF := Equivalence_Faithful E).  [with Class ReflectsIsos {C D} (F : C ⟶ D) := { reflects_iso {x y} (f : x ~> y) : IsIsomorphism (fmap[F] f) → IsIsomorphism f }, Structure/Limit/Preservation.v:243]
Program Instance fobj_iso `(F : C ⟶ D) : Proper (Isomorphism ==> Isomorphism) (fobj[F]).  (* to := fmap[F] (to X); from := fmap (from X) *)

Definition EquivalenceOfCategories_op {C D : Category} {F : C ⟶ D} (E : @EquivalenceOfCategories C D F) : @EquivalenceOfCategories (C^op) (D^op) (F^op) := @Build_EquivalenceOfCategories (C^op) (D^op) (F^op) ((@quasi_inverse C D F E)^op) (equivalence_counit_op E) (equivalence_unit_op E).
Lemma FullyFaithful `(F : C ⟶ D) `{@Full _ _ F} `{@Faithful _ _ F} : ∀ x y, F x ≅ F y → x ≅ y.

statement_record.book: Guiding principle (unnumbered): categorically-defined notions are invariant under equivalence. Bulleted claims: (1) an arrow of C is an isomorphism iff its image under an equivalence C ⟶ D is; (2) objects of C are isomorphic iff their images under an equivalence are; (3) a category equivalent to a locally small category is locally small; (4) a category equivalent to a groupoid is a groupoid; (5) C ≃ D implies C^op ≃ D^op; (6) a product of categories is equivalent to the product of any pair of equivalent categories. A definition failing equivalence-invariance is 'evil'; isomorphism-of-objects-as-equality and discreteness are the examples given.
statement_record.intree: Claim (1): both directions are proven — `fobj_iso : Proper (Isomorphism ==> Isomorphism) (fobj[F])` for any functor gives preservation, and `equivalence_reflects_isos : ReflectsIsos F` (via `ff_reflects_isos`, since every equivalence is Full and Faithful by `Equivalence_Full`/`Equivalence_Faithful`) gives reflection. Claim (2): `fobj_iso` forward, `FullyFaithful : ∀ x y, F x ≅ F y → x ≅ y` backward. Claim (5): `EquivalenceOfCategories_op`. Claims (3), (4), (6) are unstated. The general principle itself is stated only in prose (Theory/Equivalence.v:88-100, 'Equivalence is instead exactly the sameness categorical language respects … the properties it does not preserve are the ones the principle of equivalence brands "evil"'); Structure/Discrete.v:19-22 likewise records in prose that its own `Discrete` predicate (object EQUALITY, not iso) 'violates the principle of equivalence'.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same for claims (1), (2) and (5); intree-weaker overall: claims (3), (4) and (6) have no in-tree counterpart, and the 'evil'/equivalence-invariance principle is documented but never asserted. Note also that claim (1)'s reflection direction is derived from Full+Faithful, where the in-tree `Full` is the split, choice-carrying form (a chosen section `prefmap` with `fmap_sur`) rather than bare surjectivity of the hom-map — constructively a stronger hypothesis than the book's, classically the same.

gap: Three of the six bulleted claims are absent. (a) 'equivalent to a locally small category ⇒ locally small': the library has NO smallness or local-smallness predicate on categories (`rg -i 'locally small' -g '*.v'` returns 4 comment-only hits, in Functor/Hom.v, Functor/Representable.v, Structure/Complete.v, Construction/Enriched.v); universe polymorphism makes every in-tree category locally small by construction, so the claim would first need a size predicate to be stated. (b) 'equivalent to a groupoid ⇒ groupoid': there is no Groupoid PREDICATE — Construction/Groupoid.v defines only the core construction `Groupoid (C : Category) : Category` — so the claim cannot be stated. (c) 'product of a pair of categories is equivalent to the product of any pair of equivalent categories': `Functor/Construction/Product.v:34 ProductFunctor` builds F ∏⟶ G : C ∏ J ⟶ D ∏ K and `Instance/Cat/Cartesian.v:39 Cat_Cartesian` makes Cat cartesian, but no lemma says a product of two equivalences is an equivalence (grep over every file mentioning `EquivalenceOfCategories` finds no product construction). statement_record.book: Exercise 1.5.iii: prove Lemma 1.5.10 — for f : a → b and isomorphisms u : a ≅ a', v : b ≅ b' there is a UNIQUE f' : a' → b' making any one, equivalently all four, of the displayed squares (built from u or u⁻¹ and v or v⁻¹) commute, and explicitly f' = v ∘ f ∘ u⁻¹.
statement_record.intree: `iso_from_natural (i : x ≅ y) (j : x' ≅ y') (f : x ~> x') (g : y ~> y') : g ∘ to i ≈ to j ∘ f → f ∘ from i ≈ from j ∘ g` — instantiated at i := u, j := v, f := f, g := f' this is exactly 'square (1) f' ∘ u ≈ v ∘ f implies square (4) f ∘ u⁻¹ ≈ v⁻¹ ∘ f''; applying it again at iso_sym gives the converse. `premon_square_from` is the same statement re-proved verbatim in Structure/Premonoidal.v, and `iso_conj_from` is its 2-cell analogue in a bicategory. The conjugated formula itself appears only as an inline definition — Theory/Equivalence/FullFaithful.v:71 `fmap := fun d d' g => prefmap (from (eso_iso d') ∘ g ∘ to (eso_iso d))` — never as a named lemma with an existence/uniqueness statement.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the transposition between one PAIR of the four squares is proven (and only as a structure-specific helper, twice), never the four-way equivalence as such; and neither the existence claim f' := v ∘ f ∘ u⁻¹ nor the UNIQUENESS of f' is stated anywhere.

statement_record.book: Exercise 1.5.iv: show that a full and faithful functor F : C ⟶ D both REFLECTS isomorphisms — if f is a morphism of C with Ff invertible in D then f is invertible in C — and CREATES isomorphisms — if Fx ≅ Fy in D then x ≅ y in C. By Lemma 1.3.8 the converse implications hold for any functor.
statement_record.intree: Part (i): `ff_reflects_isos : ReflectsIsos F` under Context `{Full F} `{Faithful F}, i.e. `∀ {x y} (f : x ~> y), IsIsomorphism (fmap[F] f) → IsIsomorphism f`, with the inverse produced as `ff_iso_inverse f I := prefmap (two_sided_inverse I)` and the two inverse laws proven at Theory/Equivalence/Limit.v:313 and :324. Part (ii): `FullyFaithful `(F : C ⟶ D) `{Full F} `{Faithful F} : ∀ x y, F x ≅ F y → x ≅ y`. Converse (Lemma 1.3.8): `fobj_iso `(F : C ⟶ D) : Proper (Isomorphism ==> Isomorphism) (fobj[F])`, which is exactly 'any functor sends isomorphic objects to isomorphic objects, carrying an iso f to fmap f'.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same — both halves are proven at full generality, in setoid form (inverse laws up to ≈), with the converse also available. One hypothesis-strength caveat, noted rather than counted against it: the in-tree `Full` (Theory/Functor.v:331) is the split, choice-carrying form — a chosen section `prefmap` with `fmap_sur : fmap[F] (prefmap g) ≈ g` — rather than a bare surjectivity proposition on hom-sets, so constructively the hypothesis is slightly stronger than the book's (classically equivalent). This is the library's uniform house style for surjectivity, and both proofs genuinely need the chosen preimage.
